'''Ivica Zubac''' ({{IPAc-en|ɪ|v|ˈ|iː|t|s|ə|_|ˈ|z|uː|b|ɑː|t|s|}} {{respell|iv|EET|sə|_|ZOO|bahts}}; {{IPA|hr|îʋitsa zǔːbats|lang}}; born 18 March 1997) is a Croatian professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Indiana Pacers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) and the [[Croatian national basketball team]]. He was drafted by the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] in the second round in the [[2016 NBA draft]]. He played for the Lakers until the 2019 trade deadline when he was traded to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]]. During the [[2021 NBA Playoffs]], he helped the Clippers reach the [[NBA conference finals|Western Conference Finals]] for the first time in franchise history. At the 2026 trade deadline, he was acquired by the Pacers.

==Early life==
Zubac was born in [[Mostar]], [[Bosnia and Herzegovina]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Croatia |url=http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/team/p/sid/11484/tid/2168/_/2015_U18_European_Championship_Men/index.html |website=fiba.com |access-date=18 April 2025 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170717133141/http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/team/p/sid/11484/tid/2168/_/2015_U18_European_Championship_Men/index.html |archive-date=17 July 2017}}</ref> He grew up in [[Čitluk]], just east of the [[Bosnia and Herzegovina–Croatia relations|Croatian border]].<ref name=lakers17>{{Cite web|last=Trudell|first=Mike|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/news/170216-history-future-of-ivica-zubac|title=The History and Future of Ivica Zubac|website=NBA.com|date=16 February 2017|access-date=3 February 2022}}</ref> He holds dual citizenship but identifies fully as Croatian.<ref name="lakers17" />

==Professional career==

===Europe (2013–2016)===
Zubac came through the [[youth system]] of [[KK Cibona|Cibona]] and then played for Zrinjevac in the second Croatian division during the 2013–14 season. He made the roster of Cibona's men's team the following season, becoming a part of a group of prospects including [[Nik Slavica]] and [[Ante Žižić]] after the departure of [[Dario Šarić]]. Zubac played in Croatia's top-tier level [[HT Premijer liga|A-1 League]] and the [[ABA League]] his first year, and also saw action in the [[FIBA Europe Cup]] his second year.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fibaeurope.com/fibaeuropecup/compID_BYg5Rb55Jw-G5I3MZ6JB01.season_2016.roundID_11866.teamID_1444.playerID_108416.html|title=Ivica Zubac {{!}} FIBA Europe Cup|work=FIBAEurope.com|access-date=1 April 2016}}</ref> In February 2016, he left Cibona because of the financial difficulties of the team, and signed with [[KK Mega Basket|Mega Leks]] of Serbia.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.novosti.rs/vesti/sport.295.html:591198-Zubac-posvadjao-Cibonu-i-Cedevitu-a-potpisao-za-Mega-Leks|title=Zubac posvađao Cibonu i Cedevitu, a potpisao za Mega Leks|work=Novosti.rs|date=16 February 2016|access-date=1 April 2016|language=sr}}</ref>

===Los Angeles Lakers (2016–2019)===
[[File:Ivica Zubac 2016.jpg|thumb|Zubac with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] during [[NBA Summer League]] 2016]]
On 23 June 2016, Zubac was selected with the 32nd overall pick in the [[2016 NBA draft]] by the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/news/160623_ivaca-zubac-draft|title=Lakers Draft Ivica Zubac with 32nd Overall Pick|work=NBA.com|date=23 June 2016|access-date=7 July 2016}}</ref> On 7 July, he signed with the Lakers and joined the team for the [[2016 NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/160707clarksondengzubac|title=Lakers Sign Clarkson, Deng, and Zubac|work=NBA.com|date=7 July 2016|access-date=7 July 2016}}</ref> Zubac made his NBA debut on 2 November 2016, scoring six points as the fill-in starter for [[Timofey Mozgov]], as the Lakers defeated the [[Atlanta Hawks]] 123–116.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899509|title=Williams lifts Lakers to 123-116 comeback win over Hawks|work=ESPN.com|date=2 November 2016|access-date=3 November 2016}}</ref> After appearing in only 10 NBA games over the first half of the season, Zubac had a season-best game on 17 January 2017 against the [[Denver Nuggets]]. He put together his first double-double, scoring 11 points and pulling down a team-high 13 rebounds. He also had three blocked shots in the 127–121 loss.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900047|title=Jokic scores 29, Nuggets hold off struggling Lakers 127-121|work=ESPN.com|date=17 January 2017|access-date=18 January 2017}}</ref> On 12 March 2017, Zubac had 10 points, six rebounds and a season-high four blocked shots in a 118–116 loss to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/playe017–2018/seasonrs/z/zubaciv01/gamelog/2017/|title=Ivica Zubac 2016-17 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=14 March 2017}}</ref> The following night, he had a season-best game with a career-best 25 points on 12-of-15 shooting to go with 11 rebounds in a 129–101 loss to the [[Denver Nuggets]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Ramirez|first=Joey|url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/news/170313-postgame-wrap-lakers-nuggets|title=Zubac Shines Despite Loss to Denver|work=NBA.com|date=13 March 2017|access-date=14 March 2017}}</ref> On 31 March 2017, Zubac was ruled out for the rest of the season with a high ankle sprain in his right ankle.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/170331-zubac-injury-update|title=Ivica Zubac Injury Update|work=NBA.com|date=31 March 2017|access-date=31 March 2017}}</ref> During his rookie season, Zubac had multiple assignments with the [[Los Angeles D-Fenders]], the Lakers' [[NBA Development League|D-League]] affiliate.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/assignments/|title=2016-17 NBA Assignments|work=NBA.com|access-date=8 December 2016|archive-date=26 January 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170126075350/http://dleague.nba.com/assignments/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

During the 2017–18 season, Zubac had multiple assignments with the [[South Bay Lakers]], the Lakers' [[NBA G League]] affiliate due to limited playing time in the regular season.

=== Los Angeles Clippers (2019–2026) ===
On 7 February 2019, Zubac and [[Michael Beasley]] were traded to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] in exchange for [[Mike Muscala]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/clippers/la-clippers-acquire-ivica-zubac-and-michael-beasley|title=L.A. Clippers Acquire Ivica Zubac And Michael Beasley|work=NBA.com|date=7 February 2019|access-date=7 February 2019}}</ref> Zubac became a key member for the Clippers during the final stretch of the season, eventually reaching the playoffs for the first time in his career with them. Following the season, Zubac re-signed with the Clippers on a four-year, $28 million contract.<ref>{{cite web |date=July 6, 2019 |title=Zubac agrees to 4-year, $28M deal with Clippers |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/27134064/zubac-agrees-4-year-28m-deal-clippers |access-date=April 17, 2026 |publisher=espn.com}}</ref>

On 22 February 2020, Zubac posted a season-high 15 rebounds in 20 minutes of play against the Sacramento Kings.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/clippers-ivica-zubac-season-high-15-boards-in-loss/ |title=Clippers' Ivica Zubac: Season-high 15 boards in loss |website=Cbssports.com |date=24 February 2020}}</ref> In a win over the [[Houston Rockets]], Zubac shot a perfect 6 for 6 from the field and made a season-high 17 points, while also collecting 12 rebounds and blocking 1 shot on 5 March.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/clippers-ivica-zubac-perfect-from-field/ |title=Clippers' Ivica Zubac: Perfect from field |website=Cbssports.com |date=6 March 2020}}</ref>
On 6 August 2020, Zubac posted 21 points and 15 rebounds on 100% shooting in 24 minutes on the court in the 126–111 win against the [[Dallas Mavericks]]. This made Zubac the first player in the shot clock era to accomplish 20+ points and 15+ rebounds on 100% shooting in under 30 minutes of playing time.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.clipsnation.com/2020/8/7/21358790/ivica-zubac-los-angeles-clippers-nba-news-rumors/ |title=Ivica Zubac is ready to take his game to the next level |website=Clipsnation.com |date=7 August 2020 }}</ref>

On 15 February 2021, Zubac scored a season high 22 points, alongside grabbing 8 rebounds, in a 125–118 win over the [[Miami Heat]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401267585|title=Heat vs. Clippers - Game Recap - February 15, 2021|website=ESPN.com|access-date=3 February 2022}}</ref> On 14 April, Zubac recorded a [[double-double]] with 18 points and 13 rebounds in a 100–98 win over the [[Detroit Pistons]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/202104140DET.html|title=Los Angeles Clippers at Detroit Pistons Box Score, April 14, 2021|website=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=3 February 2022}}</ref>

On 19 January 2022, Zubac scored a career-high 32 points and grabbed 10 rebounds during a 130–128 overtime loss against the [[Denver Nuggets]].<ref>{{cite web | last=Swanson | first=Mirjam | title=Nikola Jokic, Nuggets edge Clippers in OT | website=Orange County Register | date=2022-01-20 | url=https://www.ocregister.com/2022/01/19/nikola-jokic-nuggets-edge-clippers-in-ot/ | access-date=2025-12-09}}</ref> During the [[2021-22 NBA season]] as a whole, Zubac started a career-high 76 games and averaged career-highs of 10.3 points and 8.5 rebounds per game.<ref>[https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/z/zubaciv01.html#per_game Ivica Zubac Per Game Stats]</ref>

On 28 June 2022, Zubac signed a three-year, $33 million contract extension with the Clippers.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Clippers agree to contract extension with center Ivica Zubac |url=https://www.nba.com/news/clippers-agree-to-contract-extension-with-center-ivica-zubac |access-date=29 June 2022 |website=NBA.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=Ivica Zubac, Clippers agree to 3-year, $33 million extension: Source |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4169997/2022/06/28/ivica-zubac-clippers-agree-to-3-year-33-million-extension-source/ |access-date=29 June 2022 |website=The Athletic |last1=Murray |first1=Law }}</ref> On 27 November, Zubac put up 31 points and a career-high 29 rebounds in a 114–110 win over the [[Indiana Pacers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/clippers-ivica-zubac-has-historic-night-with-31-points-and-29-rebounds-in-114-110-win-over-pacers/|title=Clippers' Ivica Zubac has historic night with 31 points and 29 rebounds in 114-110 win over Pacers|website=CBS Sports|last=Kaskey-Blomain|first=Michael|date=27 November 2022|access-date=27 November 2022}}</ref>

On 21 April 2024, Zubac scored a playoff career-high 20 points and 15 rebounds in a 109–97 victory against the [[Dallas Mavericks]].<ref>{{Cite magazine|last=Afseth|first=Grant|url=https://www.si.com/nba/mavericks/news/dallas-mavericks-game-1-playoffs-ivica-zubac-los-angeles-clippers-x-factor|title=Dallas Mavericks Must Improve Handling 'X-Factor' Ivica Zubac in Game 2 vs. Clippers|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=22 April 2024|access-date=26 April 2024}}</ref>

On 30 August 2024, Zubac agreed to a three–year, $58.6 million contract extension with the Clippers.<ref>{{Cite web |date=30 August 2024 |title=Clippers sign C Ivica Zubac to three-year, $58.6 million extension |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/nba/article/report-clippers-sign-c-ivica-zubac-to-three-year-58-6-million-extension/ |access-date=1 September 2024 |website=Sportsnet}}</ref> He improved significantly this year, averaging career high in rebounds and points, leading to Lakers star [[LeBron James]] wishing he had him back, considering his remarkable improvement.<ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EKN0vstk0M0 |title=LeBron was hyped to see Zubac & tells him "We need a big!" then later Zubac reveals what LBJ said |date=2025-01-20 |last=DrSwish |access-date=2025-02-24 |via=YouTube}}</ref> On 9 April 2025, Zubac recorded his first career triple-double with 20 points, 11 rebounds, and 10 assists in a 134–117 win over the [[2024–25 Houston Rockets season|Houston Rockets]].<ref>{{Cite web |first=Broderick |last=Turner |date=9 April 2025 |title=Ivica Zubac delivers first triple-double as playoff-focused Clippers beat Rockets |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/article/ivica-zubac-delivers-first-triple-050236428.html |publisher=Yahoo Sports |work=Los Angeles Times |accessdate=10 April 2025}}</ref> He started all 80 of his appearances for Los Angeles during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], averaging 16.8 points, 12.6 rebounds, and 2.7 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Ivica Zubac 2024–25 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4017837/type/nba/year/2025|access-date=February 11, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref>

Zubac made 43 appearances (including 42 starts) for the Clippers in the [[2025–26 NBA season]], recording averages of 14.4 points, 11.0 rebounds, and 2.2 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Ivica Zubac 2025–26 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4017837/type/nba/year/2026|access-date=February 11, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref>

=== Indiana Pacers (2026–present) ===
On 5 February 2026, Zubac and [[Kobe Brown]] were traded to the [[Indiana Pacers]] in exchange for [[Bennedict Mathurin]], [[Isaiah Jackson (basketball)|Isaiah Jackson]], two first-round picks, and a second-round pick.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/indiana-pacers-acquire-ivica-zubac-and-kobe-brown-from-los-angeles-clippers|title=Indiana Pacers Acquire Ivica Zubac and Kobe Brown from Los Angeles Clippers|work=NBA.com|date=5 February 2026|access-date=6 February 2026}}</ref> One of the picks would turn out to be the 5th pick in the [[2026 NBA Draft]], where the Clippers used the pick to draft [[Keaton Wagler]]. <ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/news/2026-nba-draft-order|title=2026 NBA Draft Results: Picks 1-60|work=NBA|date=23 June 2026|access-date=23 June 2026}}</ref> Following his trade, head coach [[Rick Carlisle]] stated that Zubac would have a delayed debut due to an ankle injury and a paternity leave.<ref name="espn-zubac-pacers-debut">{{Cite web|title=Zubac has strong Pacers debut despite ankle ‘tweak,’ Carlisle says|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/47853936/zubac-pacers-debut-hold-ankle-heals-carlisle-says|access-date=2026-02-08|website=[[ESPN]]|language=en-US}}</ref><ref name="yahoo-zubac-baby" /> He started five games for Indiana, logging averages of 11.6 points, 7.2 rebounds, and 1.8 assists. On 26 March, Zubac was ruled out for the season after suffering a [[fractured rib]] during a game against the [[2025–26 Portland Trail Blazers season|Portland Trail Blazers]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Ivica Zubac out for season after suffering fractured rib |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/nba-news/1946197/ivica-zubac-out-for-season-after-suffering-fractured-rib/ |website=Eurohoops |access-date=30 March 2026 |language=en |date=20 March 2026}}</ref> The Zubac trade ended up costing the Pacers the 5th overall pick in the 2026 NBA draft lottery. <ref>{{Cite news |last=Henderson |first=Devon |date=2026-05-10 |title=Pacers’ Kevin Pritchard apologizes to fans for draft lottery gamble gone wrong |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7268783/2026/05/10/kevin-pritchard-apology-pacers-clippers-lottery-trade/ |access-date=2026-05-10 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref>

==National team career ==
Zubac represented the Croatian junior national team during the [[2013 FIBA Europe Under-16 Championship]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fibaeurope.com/compID_YUjW-7-FJ,kK9s431Lyr41.season_2013.roundID_9441.playerID_108416.teamID_2168.html|title=Ivica Zubac {{!}} U16 European Championship Men (2013) {{!}} FIBA Europe|work=FIBAEurope.com|access-date=1 April 2016}}</ref> He averaged 17.6 points and 7.9 rebounds a contest during the [[2015 FIBA Under-19 World Championship]] in Greece,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fiba.basketball/world/u19/2015/player/Ivica-Zubac|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150702083125/http://www.fiba.com/world/u19/2015/Ivica-ZUBAC|url-status=live|archive-date=2 July 2015|title=Ivica ZUBAC at the Players of the 2015 FIBA U19 World Championship |website=FIBA.com|access-date=1 April 2016}}</ref> while receiving All-World Championship Under-19 Second Team honors from the European basketball website ''[[eurobasket.com]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.eurobasket.com/World-Championships-U19/basketball_2015_Men.aspx|title=World Championships U19 2015 - Men Basketball|work=Eurobasket.com|access-date=1 April 2016|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160414131457/http://www.eurobasket.com/World-Championships-U19/basketball_2015_Men.asp|archive-date=14 April 2016}}</ref> Zubac averaged double digits in scoring (15.8 points per game) and rebounding (12.9 rebounds per game), to go along with 3.0 blocks per game at the [[2015 FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://u18men.fibaeurope.com/en/compID_8aYeHlfuGF-mF5IqO8aFH1.season_2015.roundID_11484.teamID_2168.playerID_108416.html|title=Ivica Zubac {{!}} U18 Europe Championship Men - Division A|work=FIBAEurope.com|access-date=1 April 2016|archive-date=31 July 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160731213841/http://u18men.fibaeurope.com/en/compID_8aYeHlfuGF-mF5IqO8aFH1.season_2015.roundID_11484.teamID_2168.playerID_108416.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> while making the all-tournament second team (as selected by ''eurobasket.com'').<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.eurobasket.com/European-Championships-U18/basketball_2015.aspx|title=European Championships U18 2015 - Men Basketball|work=Eurobasket.com|access-date=1 April 2016}}</ref>
